status: authored 2026-10-09; the recipes are closed by tools/player_waystone.py into build/datapacks/cobblers_player_waystone (world-local, load-time, no functions); the gift is Oak's, a grant_reward_once in data/quests.json main_worldshift_reveal (transition grant_oak_waystone). Valid output only: nothing here has been seen in a game
decision: the owner, 2026-10-09: "a player's own waystone, given by Oak once after the starter ... so a player can make a house anywhere: one per player, its crafting recipe closed ..., and its pickup on break kept so a player who moves keeps one."
rung: Cobblemon/addon/Cobbleverse dependency as shipped (the Waystones mod's own block and its default break drop), a datapack for the closed recipes (Fabric API's fabric:load_conditions, the pattern tools/key_ball.py uses for the Beast Ball), and the dialogue/reward system for the gift (grant_reward_once). No config key changes, no script, no mod.

gift.when: in Oak's own conversation, after the starter is chosen, the rules are recorded and the send-off is given (oak_003): two lines (oak_waystone_001, oak_waystone_002) before the permanent repeat line. A player Oak already sent off, before this shipped, is offered it on their next talk by an entry rule (priority 6), once, and the claim is permanent
gift.once: claim_field is a player boolean; the grant is guarded by it and writes it only when every give reported success (tools/compile_dialogue.py grant_reward_once). One per player, ever: a second one is not on offer
gift.keep_on_break: no loot table is overridden. The jar's data/waystones/loot_table/blocks/waystone.json drops waystones:waystone for the lower half on any break that survives an explosion, with no tool condition (silk touch only copies the block entity); a player's own waystone, broken, is an item again, and the mod's WaystoneBlockBase.playerWillDestroy removes its registry entry (class strings, read from the jar; not run), so a player who moves picks it up and sets it down elsewhere
gift.wording: Oak's two lines are a placeholder in his voice for Codex to replace; they carry no rule a player needs to read

groups.placeable waystones (11 recipes, 10 item: waystone, mossy (three recipes), sandy, blackstone, deepslate, end_stone, mud_bricks, prismarine, purpur, red_nether_bricks: each is a block a player could place, which is a new waystone anywhere
groups.sharestones (16): placeable; every one of a colour links to the others of that colour, a private network
groups.portstones (16): placeable; each is a warp target a player names and links, a private network
groups.warp plate (1): placeable pad that warps to a chosen waystone
groups.warp items (6): warp_stone (to any activated waystone from anywhere), warp_scroll, return_scroll (back to the last waystone used), portal_scroll, twinbound_feather, epitaph: each moves a player between waystones, which is the fast travel the owner limits
groups.ingredients (4): blank_scroll, warp_dust, dormant_shard, deepslate_shard: only ever made into the items above; closed so nothing half-made is left to find a use

config_facts.file: base-pack/cobbleverse/config/waystones-common.toml (the Cobbleverse default; there is no overlay of it in modpack/config/ or server/config/, so this is what the server runs)

keys.general.restrictedWaystones: ["PLAYER"]: waystones of origin PLAYER may be edited only by their owner (the file's own comment: "PLAYER is special in that it allows only edits by the owner of the waystone")
keys.general.defaultVisibility: "ACTIVATION": a newly placed waystone is usable by whoever has activated it, not global
keys.general.allowedVisibilities: [ ]: no player may set GLOBAL, so a player cannot publish theirs to everyone
keys.teleports.enableCosts: false: a warp costs no XP and no item. warpRequirements (scaled_add_xp_cost(distance, 0.01) capped at 27, interdimensional 27) is therefore inert
keys.teleports.enableCooldowns: false: no cooldown; the inventory button's 300 tick cooldown is inert too
keys.worldGen.chunksBetweenWildWaystones / sp: 25 / REGULAR: wild and village waystones generate in NEW chunks; the world is a pre-exported map inside its border, so none is expected (data/hub_waystones.json does_not_cover). Left as shipped: not decided by the owner

reading.other_players_can_use_a_players_waystone: yes, unless private: with ACTIVATION visibility another player who finds it and right-clicks it activates it for themselves and can warp to it (they cannot edit or rename it). The config offers no private setting: its only visibility switch is allowedVisibilities, whose own comment names GLOBAL alone, and it is empty. The jar's WaystoneVisibility enum also lists TEAM and SHARD_ONLY (class strings); whether the edit screen lets a player pick either was not read and is not run. Read as shipped, a player's house waystone is one anyone who walks up to it and right-clicks it can use (from the config comments and docs/world-building/NAVIGATION.md section 2; not run in a game)
reading.gym_town_and_hub_waystones_and_the_badge: the badge rule is off (data/progression.json waystone_gate.enforced false, the owner 2026-10-05): a badge pre-activates its own town's waystone and nothing is forgotten without one, so a gym-town waystone is also activated by a visit. A hub waystone (data/hub_waystones.json) is a visit only. Neither is gated by a badge for use

does_not_cover: a town or hub waystone broken by a player in survival drops the same item, so a second player waystone is possible by taking one from a town; nothing in this repository protects the town waystones from being broken (not measured: whether the world's spawn or town areas are protected)
a creative-mode or operator `give` of any waystones item
a player who loses theirs (lava, void, a death that drops it) has no second grant; the claim is permanent by design
wild or village waystones in new chunks (config above) and the guaranteed-waystone worldgen modifiers the jar ships under data/waystones/lithostitched
